title: Angels and Judgment
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Angels are sometimes involved in God’s righteous judgment and final purposes. They do not judge independently, but carry out the command of the holy God.
summary: Angels are sometimes involved in God’s righteous judgment and final purposes. They do not judge independently, but carry out the command of the holy God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ will return with His angels in glory and judge with perfect righteousness. Angelic judgment serves His authority, not their own power.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture sometimes shows angels carrying out acts of judgment. This reveals that God’s heavenly servants execute His will not only in comfort and protection, but also in righteous judgment.

Angels are involved in final judgment imagery. Jesus teaches that angels will gather out of His kingdom those who do evil, and He will come with His angels in glory.

This doctrine must be handled with sobriety. Angels do not act from cruelty or independent authority. Their role in judgment belongs to the larger truth that God is holy and will judge evil rightly.

Christ is the center of final judgment. Angels accompany and serve, but Jesus is the appointed Judge and King.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often prefer to think of angels only as comforting figures. Scripture gives a fuller picture. The servants of a holy God also serve His righteous judgment.

This doctrine reminds believers that judgment is real and that God’s holiness must not be softened. It also strengthens confidence that evil will not be ignored forever.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let the biblical picture of angels deepen reverence before God. Do not sentimentalize the unseen realm. Worship the holy Lord, proclaim the Gospel with urgency, and trust that Christ will judge evil with perfect righteousness.
